intro.text: April 13, 1970. Apollo 13 is about 330,000 km from Earth, two days into a smooth flight to the Moon.

cutscene.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): subtitle timings once e1_problem.mp3 is trimmed. The words below are the 55:55:20 to 55:55:42 exchange.

shots.caption: A bang, then the master alarm.

A panel blows off the Service Module.
Oxygen vents into the sunlight.

subtitles.text: Swigert: “Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here.”
Lousma: “This is Houston. Say again, please.”
Lovell: “Houston, we've had a problem. We've had a main B bus undervolt.”

shots.caption: The crew moves into Aquarius, their lifeboat.

poll.question: The lifeboat is short on power. Do we keep the crew warm?

options.label: Save power
options.good: more battery for the trip home.
options.cost: the cabin gets close to freezing.

options.label: Keep a heater on
options.good: a warmer crew that sleeps better.
options.cost: less battery for the trip home.

captions.text: A 34-second burn puts them back on a path that loops around the Moon and home.
Behind the Moon, radio contact is lost for about 25 minutes.

On the far-side pass, they are farther from Earth than any humans before them.
A distance record that stood until Artemis II in 2026.

shots.caption: Aquarius swings around the far side of the Moon.
The ship is still one stack: Odyssey, then Aquarius.
Radio contact with Houston is restored at about 77:33.
The burn home, called PC+2, is set for GET 079:27:39.

subtitles.text: Houston and the crew count through the burn.

poll.question: We've come around the Moon. How fast do we go home?

options.label: Normal speed
options.cost: a longer trip in the cold lifeboat.

options.label: Fastest way home
options.cost: we drop the damaged back half of the ship, leaving the heat shield exposed.
options.note: Considered in 1970 and rejected, because the Service Module protected the heat shield from the cold of space.

captions.text: CO2 is climbing. The LM's scrubbers were sized for two people.

shots.caption: The CO2 caution light comes on.
The square canisters don't fit the round sockets.

Two lithium hydroxide canisters, gray tape, bags from two cooling garments,
an LM cue card, suit hoses and a sock.

subtitles.text: Kerwin begins reading the procedure at about 90:22.

poll.question: CO2 is building up. Houston's fix isn't fully tested yet.

options.label: Wait for Houston
options.good: a tested design that seals well.
options.cost: CO2 climbs higher while we wait.

options.label: Build it now
options.cost: a tired crew and a leaky seal.

captions.text: Haise: “Our do-it-yourself lithium hydroxide canister change is complete.”

shots.caption: To save power, almost everything is switched off.
The cabin is dark, cold and wet.
Water isn't just for drinking. It cools the electronics too.

poll.question: Water also cools the electronics. How much should the crew drink?

options.label: Very little
options.good: more water to cool the electronics.

captions.text:
A 14-second course correction at 105:18:28,
steered by keeping Earth's day/night line steady in the window.

At about 112:12, Aquarius starts recharging Odyssey's reentry batteries.
It takes about 15 hours.

poll.question: The landing capsule is frozen and wet inside. When do we switch it on?

shots.caption: The crew lets the Service Module go and sees the damage.

subtitles.text: Lovell: “And there's one whole side of that spacecraft missing.”

Lovell: “Right by the high gain antenna, the whole panel is blown out,
almost from the base to the engine.”

steps.title: LM jettison
captions: Kerwin: “Farewell, Aquarius, and we thank you.”

steps.title: Blackout
captions: Radio blackout lasted about six minutes, roughly a minute and a half longer than expected.
steps.heat_shield_text: The heat shield had been exposed to space for the whole trip home.

scorecard.title: Every path brings them home. How much margin did you leave them?

rows.label: Drinking water per person
rows.history: About 0.18 L (6 oz) a day, a fifth of normal

rows.label: Haise's infection
rows.history: Yes, a urinary tract infection with fever

rows.label: Heat shield exposed
rows.history: No, the Service Module stayed attached until near the end

scorecard.closing: The real crew made it home with almost nothing to spare.
